The pattern is consistent: wherever there was a hard‑coded emoji (e.g., "🔧", "▶", "👍", "⭐"), I've swapped it for `${icon('name', size)}` and updated any related text handling.

```html
<button class="btn green" id="new-go">+ Create Place</button>
```

The plus sign is an emoji (actually a plain plus character). To keep the UI consistent and leverage the icon system, I should replace that `+` with the `plus` icon. The icon name `plus` is already defined in `icons.js` (it was added earlier when I added the `ban` icon; the file now contains both `coin` and `ban`, but the `plus` icon is part of the existing set). I need to choose a suitable size – most other inline icons in buttons use sizes around 14‑16 pixels, and the play button uses 16, while the like/favorite icons use 14. A 14‑pixel plus should match the visual weight of the other button icons.

Thus, the edit should target the exact snippet containing the button markup. I'll replace the literal `+` with `${icon('plus', 14)}` while preserving the surrounding text "Create Place". No other changes are needed for this line.

I'll construct an Edit tool call with `replace_all: false`, specifying the file path `/home/lane/rblx/public/js/app.js`, the old string (the two lines of HTML for the input and button), and the new string where the button's inner HTML now includes the icon.

This will complete the migration of all remaining emoji symbols to the SVG icon system, ensuring a uniform look across the app.
